entries.description: Land trust that has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon, jointly described with California Women's Land Trust; aims to hold land for all women and children, remove it from the speculative market, and help women set up local land trusts.
entries.raw_text: LAND TRUSTS FOR WOMEN is an effort to give women control over their own destinies. Two groups of women have researched the concept of land trusts, and formed groups to acquire land for all women and children at all times. This would promote the spiritual, emotional, physical, cultural, and economic well-being of women, and preserve the land. Many of us love nature deeply, and need to live with green all around us and be self-sufficient. We feel caged in polluted, violent cities where we survive day to day by doing meaningless work or by standing in welfare lines. Financially poor women are unable to buy rural property. Private ownership creates hassles anyway. Putting land in a land trust removes it from the speculative market. It would be available to all women and children, whether they want to live there or just stop for a short time, camp out, and relax. We can help women set up local land trusts, or they can join us. Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon. Write OWLT, Box 1713, Eugene, OR, 97401, or California Women's Land Trust, c/o Carole & Yolanda, 1538 N. St. Andrews, Hollywood, CA, 90028.
entries.notes: Listed jointly with California Women's Land Trust in one paragraph; each gets its own row. Type Land Trust: 'formed groups to acquire land' and 'Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres'. Acreage 145 is the OWLT figure. Accepted groups: 'all women and children' before 1986 means Lesbian women + Non-lesbian women, Girl children + Boy children. Focuses: 'be self-sufficient' (Farming/self-sufficiency); 'preserve the land', 'live with green all around us' (Environmentalism/eco-friendly). PO box so land street/zip blank; land state OR from 'southern Oregon'. Residents not stated.

entries.description: Group that has 'secured' 80 undeveloped acres in northwest Arkansas as a beginning for a women's land trust and is still researching how to form one; lives only with dykes, relates to female children only, wants to stress farming; open to women staying full-time or briefly, who must work; seeks money to pay off the land and gather tools.
entries.raw_text: WOMEN ON LAND has "secured" 80 acres of land in northwest Arkansas as a beginning for a women's land trust. We are investigating and researching the details of how to form a land trust. We believe a land trust is a way each woman involved with this land can have equal access and responsibility to the land to the feminist community. The concept of a land trust can take care of legal trips and power trips. The land can be legally "owned" by the land trust and each woman could have lease for lifetime use of the land. There is much to be worked out, but we want you to know that no woman woman will get ripped off after putting in her time, energy, work, or money. It is difficult to review all the research and energy into laws, qualifying to fit their rules, and at the same time, trying to build a new culture, but we have to use their laws for some measure of protection against them. We will live only with dykes. We wish to relate to female children only - male children would be too sexist an influence on a developing women's environment. We want to stress farming on this land to raise food to feed the women on the land and support sisters in the cities. There are no buildings on the land, just 80 acres of beautiful trees, a waterfall, a creek, and lots of painful bugs. We need to share the responsibility for getting money to pay off the land, for gathering tools, building materials, seed, horse, windmill. We are open to any woman who wants to relate to this land whether she wants to stay full-time, work for the summer, camp and work, spend the weekend, or stay here on the way cross country. We do want to emphasize the need to work. When you write, describe yourself, your politics, what you can offer and why you want to come. (No dogs please.) Send a stamped, self-addressed envelope to Women on Land, PO Box 521, Fayetteville, Arkansas, 72701.
entries.notes: Type Land Fund/Seeking Land: land is 'secured' but they are still 'investigating and researching the details of how to form a land trust' and no buildings or residents are described; not yet held in a trust. Accepted groups: 'We will live only with dykes' (Lesbian women); 'female children only' (Girl children); 'open to any woman' not coded as non-lesbian because of the dykes-only living statement. Focuses: Lesbian separatism from 'live only with dykes'; Farming/self-sufficiency from 'stress farming on this land to raise food'. Land state AR from 'northwest Arkansas'; mailing is a PO box so no street/zip. Mailing state printed as 'Arkansas'. Residents not stated. Typo 'no woman woman' kept in raw_text.

entries.land_location_as_stated: the eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington
entries.description: Small lesbian farm in an isolated valley in the Cascade foothills, started by two women and a child to rebuild an old farm as a place for all women to work, live, or visit; has an old cabin, well, chicken coop and outhouse, with a sauna, and plans more structures, an herb garden, a June festival and health workshops.
entries.raw_text: SAPPHA SURVIVAL SCHOOL is a small lesbian farm in the eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington. One woman who stayed there for a week last summer wrote the following about SSS. "Two women and one child, with many visitors, started this spring to rebuild an old farm valley into a place for all women to work and live, or visit. I helped rebuild the old cabin, later to be the community center, helped dig a well, and build a chicken coop. Freedom and Dykepride run strong - the valley is isolated enough to remove society's inhibitions and its censure of lesbians. Olivia Newton Outhouse is presently open to the sky and a valley view, stream water is pumped to flow between pine branches for the shower and half naked Amazons are everywhere! Evening relaxation is often a sauna, fueled by hot rocks and followed by a dip in the stream." This summer they planned on more structures including a children's space scaled to their size, and an outrageous playground scaled to everybody's size. They also planned an herb garden, a festival in June, and workshops on health. To find out more, write: SSS, Box 4D, Aeneas Valley Road, Tonasket, WA, 98855.
entries.notes: Type Private/Individual Land: two-woman rule, 'Two women and one child, with many visitors'; visitors do not change it and the listing does not recruit members to live there. Residents 3: two women and one child live there. Accepted groups: 'a place for all women to work and live, or visit' pre-1986 means Lesbian women + Non-lesbian women; 'one child' of unspecified sex is not coded as both, and a 'children's space' is planned, so Girl children coded only tentatively; child gender is not given, so this is a judgment. Focuses: Lesbian separatism is weakly implied by 'small lesbian farm' and 'isolated enough to remove ... censure of lesbians' (a judgment; does not state only lesbians); Farming/self-sufficiency from 'lesbian farm'; Workshops/education from 'workshops on health' and the 'Survival School' name. Land state WA from the listing; mailing address is a box on a road ('Box 4D, Aeneas Valley Road') but the town is Tonasket; land city not stated by the listing so not guessed. Acreage not given.

entries.land_location_as_stated: beautiful wilderness area of Oklahoma near Tishomingo, capitol of the chicasaw nation
entries.description: Space opening soon in Oklahoma wilderness near Tishomingo with 70 acres for camping or year-round living; women work together in recreation, farming and growing, keep their own shelter, share a community garden and horses, sell womancraft through the Magic Ferry; monthly $5.00 rate goes to pay for the land. Listing continues on the next page.
entries.raw_text: ANOTHER DEMENTION is opening soon to accomodate women who are seeking a space on the land working together with other women in areas of recreation, farming, and general growing. 70 acres will be available for camping and/or year-round living in beautiful wilderness area of Oklahoma near Tishomingo, capitol of the chicasaw nation. A variety of flora and fauna abound in the area of the wildlife refuge 3 miles away and can be enjoyed while canoeing down the blue river or pennington creek. Wild mustangs adopted through the government will be among the horses in residence eager to offer alternative means of transportation around the area for exploration and enjoyment. Womancraft can be sold in distribution outlet store on roadfront or consigned to be distributed by the MAGIC FERRY to the FERRY DYKINGS and other contact points across the country. Women in residence will maintain their own shelter and be responsible for their own life-support needs. A community garden will be the major food source operating on cooperative energy. Monthly rate for any number of days spent on the land is $5.00, payable on or before each new moon. This money will be used for payment of the land. Financial
entries.notes: Listing is cut off at the bottom of the page and continues on the next page; contact address is not on this page. Type Land Fund/Seeking Land: 'is opening soon' and the money 'will be used for payment of the land', so no community is yet living there. Acreage 70 is land 'will be available', not yet established. Accepted groups: 'women who are seeking a space' pre-1986 means Lesbian women + Non-lesbian women. Focus Farming/self-sufficiency from 'farming, and general growing' and 'community garden will be the major food source'. Womancraft sale is a passing mention, not coded as Archives/cultural work. Land city Tishomingo from 'near Tishomingo' (judgment); state OK stated.
